profile.grounding_note: Simulated coaching profile grounded in real StudentLife pre-term surveys (PSS=24.0, PHQ-9=6.0, UCLA Loneliness=32.0, PHQ-9 item 9=0, Extraversion=1.75, Neuroticism=4.25, Conscientiousness=3.56); courses: COSC 065, COSC 027.
goals: Reduce high stress (PSS=24.0) during COSC 065 and COSC 027 labs with short restorative micro-breaks
Keep a consistent evening wind-down routine without feeling pressured into heavy workouts
Break lab assignments into small, concrete next steps when feeling overwhelmed

preferences.activity_style: Quiet indoor micro-breaks (stretching, deep breathing, warm tea)

constraints: High baseline perceived stress (PSS=24.0) and neuroticism (4.25) with low extraversion (1.75)
Studies frequently in quiet campus spaces and prefers low-friction resets

episodes.final_message: With a deadline today and another coming up in 3 days, it makes sense that stress is running high tonight. Before tackling your next study block, try taking a quick 5-minute quiet reset—enjoy some warm tea or do a gentle indoor stretch away from your screen.

simulated_feedback.feedback_text: Please don't suggest running, jogging, or going to the gym—I hate working out when I have CS deadlines. I prefer quiet indoor stretching, deep breathing, or making a cup of tea.

episodes.final_message: With a deadline today and stress feeling high tonight, you've been working hard. Before starting your next task, try taking a quiet 5-minute reset to sip some warm tea or do a few slow, deep breaths away from your screen.

simulated_feedback.feedback_text: That quiet indoor break idea was much better. Also note that I study late at Baker-Berry Library, so keep suggestions library-compatible and super brief (under 35 words).

preference_updates.tone_constraint: Keep messages under 35 words and quiet/library-compatible

episodes.final_message: With today's deadline and high stress tonight, you've been working hard. Before starting your next study block at Baker-Berry, take a quiet 5-minute break to sip tea and stretch gently.

simulated_feedback.feedback_text: Thanks—concise, quiet, and fits my Baker-Berry Library study session without any gym or running suggestions.

learned_preferences.preference: NEVER suggest running, jogging, gym visits, or heavy workouts, especially around CS deadlines.
ALWAYS favor quiet indoor stretching, slow deep breathing, or taking a warm tea break for stress reduction and micro-breaks.
Keep suggestions quiet and library-compatible, suited for studying at Baker-Berry Library.
Keep coach messages super brief (strictly under 35 words).
NEVER suggest running, jogging, or gym workouts; focus on quiet indoor breaks like stretching, deep breathing, tea, or water.
NEVER suggest running, jogging, gym, or intense workouts; stick to quiet, low-intensity activities like stretching, deep breathing, or sipping tea.
When studying at Baker-Berry Library, suggest quiet, library-compatible breaks (e.g., tea, stretching, breathing pauses).
Keep coaching messages concise, ideally under 40 words.
